assertions: The route lifecycle transitions use compare-and-swap revisions and retain a bounded audit history with the acting principal.
New acceptance is rejected after draining begins and after retirement; an existing idempotent acceptance remains readable and pinned to its original route.
Retirement is refused while canonical submissions, outboxes, attempts, dispatches, effects, or result publications remain, and remains draining while the Prefect client reports an active flow run.
After canonical and remote work drain, the registrar pauses and retains the immutable deployment; reactivation verifies the deployment and Process pool before resuming it and reopening admissions.
SQLModel durable snapshot reconstruction preserves route status, revision, audit history, and workload counters without adding a provider table.

runtime.wheel_environment: Fresh-environment package origins; inherited PYTHONPATH unset and pytest source injection disabled.

limitations: This campaign uses a controlled Prefect client and SQLite provider reconstruction; it does not prove route drain, retirement, or rollback across live processes, PostgreSQL, or a self-hosted Prefect server.
Retired deployments and Prefect history are retained indefinitely; scoped orphan cleanup and its retention window remain open.
The store-wide lifecycle requires all API and worker processes to share the same durable SQLModel store_id.
